q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution

The Q2 FY2027 earnings call is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 16, 2026. That leaves **10 days** until the forward guidance is announced.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA's most recent forward guidance (provided May 20, 2026, for Q2 FY2027) was **$91.0 billion ±2%**, which translates to a range of $89.18B to $92.82B.

The most likely scenario is that the company will provide forward guidance in a similar range or slightly higher. Key considerations:

- **Recent trajectory**: Q1 FY2027 achieved $81.6 billion in actual revenue, representing 85% YoY growth
- **Sequential growth**: The $91.0B guidance for Q2 represents roughly 11.4% sequential growth from Q1's $81.6B
- **Pattern consistency**: This sequential growth rate is moderate and sustainable given the AI data center boom
- **China constraint**: The guidance explicitly does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China, which is a known constraint but already built into the $91.0B figure
- **Market conditions**: No major disruptions have been announced in the interim 10 days

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro deterioration**: Sudden economic slowdown affecting cloud provider capex plans
- **China restrictions tightening**: Further geopolitical constraints on exports
- **Competitive pressures**: Unexpected gains by AMD or custom silicon solutions
- **Supply chain issues**: Manufacturing or logistics problems limiting fulfillment
- **Demand softness**: Lower-than-expected order intake from major customers
- **Conservative guidance**: Company opts for a more cautious outlook due to uncertainty

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-expected demand**: Major cloud providers accelerating AI infrastructure buildout
- **China tariff/export relief**: Unexpected policy changes allowing some China revenue
- **Market share gains**: Continued dominance in AI accelerators despite competition
- **Product momentum**: Successful launches of new GPU generations driving additional demand
- **Customer concentration strength**: Major hyperscalers increasing orders beyond expectations
- **Optimistic outlook**: Management confidence in sustaining the growth trajectory

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**From the research provided**: NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 was $91.0 billion ±2% when announced on May 20, 2026. This is the most direct precedent available.

Historical context from the research shows:
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6 billion (85% YoY growth)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance at announcement: $91.0B ±2%

No other historical guidance revisions or patterns are provided in the research.

## Reasoning

Given that the guidance was already issued (May 20) and we're just 10 days from the earnings call where it will be formally reaffirmed or revised, the base case is that guidance remains at $91.0B ±2%.

However, companies sometimes adjust guidance at earnings announcements. The range of realistic outcomes:

- **Reaffirmation at $91.0B**: ~50% probability (management sticks with prior guidance)
- **Modest upward revision** (to $93-96B): ~25% probability (stronger sequential demand)
- **Modest downward revision** (to $88-90B): ~15% probability (cautious adjustment)
- **Significant change** (>$96B or <$88B): ~10% probability (unexpected macro shift)

The distribution should be centered around $91.0B with standard deviation of approximately $2.5B, reflecting both the ±2% range already given and potential for modest revisions.

**Median estimate**: $91.0B (the current guidance)
**10th percentile** (lower tail): $87.5B (cautious downward revision)
**90th percentile** (upper tail): $95.0B (moderate upward revision, growth momentum)

Low (10th percentile): 87500000000
Median (50th percentile): 91000000000
High (90th percentile): 95000000000

NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue was provided on May 20, 2026, during the release of their Q1 FY2027 earnings. The company expects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

NVIDIA reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion for the quarter ended April 26, 2026, an 85% increase year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). The company is set to host a conference call on August 26, 2026, to discuss its Q2 FY2027 financial results [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-sets-conference-call-for-second-quarter-financial-results-6927195).
